introducer.title: editTelemetry: preserve precise edit survival attribution

cases.mechanism: A replaying AsyncIterableSource retained every emitted change object, including both full StringText document snapshots, after the sole consumer had processed it; retained memory therefore grew with edit history for as long as document telemetry tracking remained active.
cases.symptom: Repeated edits, especially in large long-lived documents, caused monotonically growing retained heap and corresponding GC pressure.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed helper now returns a single-consumer AsyncIterableProducer. Its ProducerConsumer removes each consumed value from _unconsumedValues, while the startup buffer is explicitly cleared after transfer, so only pending changes remain retained and consumed full-document snapshots can be collected.
cases.evidence: Base line 33 constructed AsyncIterableSource for iterateObservableChanges; AsyncIterableSource delegates to AsyncIterableObject, whose _results array appends every emitted change and whose iterator advances only a private index, so consumed entries remain referenced for the stream lifetime. CombineStreamedChanges creates this stream per tracked document and each change includes value/prevValue StringText snapshots. The added GC regression test drives 80 edits while the pipeline remains active and requires all 40 sampled consumed snapshots to be collectible.
